column3: NKJV reads “in the Prophets,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “in Isaiah the prophet.”
Close to the Greek; “forgiveness” is rendered “remission.”
Close to the Greek; “tearing open” is rendered “parting.”
NKJV has “the gospel of the kingdom of God,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “the gospel of God.” “Delivering up” is rendered “was put in prison.”
Close to the Greek; “Come after Me” is rendered “Follow Me.”
NKJV has no “immediately,” as in the Textus Receptus; the critical text begins “And immediately there was ….”
NKJV includes “Let us alone!,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text begins “What have we to do with You.”
NKJV follows the Textus Receptus: “What new doctrine is this? For with authority …”; the critical text reads “A new teaching with authority!”
Close to the Greek; “news” is rendered “fame.”
